- MEDIUM `[empty-footprint-precheck]` [confidence: limited]: Step 2 (`detail --commit` footprint) and step 4 (`manifest sweep --commit` footprint) both give a reason for the new footprint dirt check that step 1 makes false. Step 2 says a whole-tree check would be wrong because "an unrelated dirty file would trigger an empty commit that fails". Step 1 says "When no entry has a change, `commit_all` makes no commit and returns success with a tail saying nothing changed". So an empty footprint can no longer fail the commit. The pre-check is still needed where a caller prints "nothing to commit" or skips a message. Step 2's `_commit_if_dirty` is one such caller, and step 4's `cmd_sweep` is the other. As written, though, a reader will think the pre-check is what prevents a failure, and may drop it or add a second, redundant check.
  - Fix: Reword the rationale in steps 2 and 4 to say the footprint dirt check only decides the caller's "nothing to commit" message and flow. Say that `commit_all` itself already returns success for an empty footprint.

- INFO `[step1-granularity-split-2e7cebc0]` [confidence: limited]: Step 1 "Change `commit_all` in `plan_tool/cli/gitcommit.py` so it takes a required `paths` argument. It stages with `git add -A -- <literal pathspecs>` and commits with `git commit -m <subject> -- <pathspecs>`, so only those paths are committed and other index entries are not swept in. A directory entry covers everything beneath it, which matches how `unexpected_dirty_paths` already treats directories. Before staging, a gitignored expected path is skipped with a one-line warning naming it, using the existing `path_is_gitignored`. After a successful commit, any non-ignored expected path that is still dirty in `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` produces a non-zero result whose tail names the path. A gitignored path skipped this way does not fail the commit. A footprint entry that is neither on disk nor tracked is skipped before staging (it names nothing to commit), and is outside the post-commit check. A tracked path deleted on disk is still staged by `-A`. An entry with no change is staged harmlessly. When no entry has a change, `commit_all` makes no commit and returns success with a tail saying nothing changed, rather than the non-zero 'nothing to commit' git would give. Existing callers keep their whole-tree behaviour for now by passing `[repo_root]` as the footprint; steps 2–5 replace that. Destructive-operation disposition: `commit_all` deletes nothing itself. Through `-A`, a delete or rename inside the footprint is still staged, and a delete outside it is no longer staged. Update the module docstring, which describes `--commit` as staging the produced edits. Unit tests go in `tests/cli/test_gitcommit.py` against a real temporary repo: an unrelated dirty file is not committed, a pre-staged unrelated file is not committed, a delete and a rename inside the footprint are staged, a directory entry stages its new nested files, an ignored path warns and the commit still succeeds, an expected path left dirty (for example when a hook rewrites it) is reported by name with a non-zero rc, an absent untracked entry is skipped without failing, a tracked deleted entry is staged, and a footprint with no changes returns success with no commit." carries refactor verb(s) ['rename'] and feature verb(s) ['add'] — likely two concerns in one step.
- INFO `[step4-granularity-split-958871d7]` [confidence: limited]: Step 4 "Give `manifest sweep --commit` in `plan_tool/cli/manifest.py` its footprint from records the sweep already returns: the manifest path, and each `ArchiveOutcome`'s original `plan_path` (a delete) and `archived_to` (an add). It also includes the source and destination of each `plan_details_moved` pair and each `duplicate_archive_results` pair. Missing-entry deregistrations are covered by the manifest path. Replace the whole-tree `working_tree_dirty` check before the commit with a check for dirt inside the footprint, so an unrelated dirty file no longer turns 'sweep moved nothing' into a commit. Destructive-operation disposition: the archive moves and the manifest rewrites themselves are unchanged. Their deletes still reach the commit through `-A`, and only what gets staged is narrowed. Rewrite the `--commit` help text ('stage all changes (git add -A)') and regenerate `docs/cli/sweep.md`. Tests go in `tests/cli/test_manifest_cmds.py`: an archived plan's move and its plan-details move are committed as renames, an unrelated dirty file is not committed, an unrelated dirty file alone gives 'nothing to commit', and the footprint is clean afterwards." carries refactor verb(s) ['move'] and feature verb(s) ['add'] — likely two concerns in one step.
- INFO `[step5-granularity-split-35023ee5]` [confidence: limited]: Step 5 "Make `paths` required on `_commit_green_step` in `plan_tool/cli/run_cmd.py` and have it delegate staging and committing to `commit_all`, so `run --commit` uses the same ignored-path warning and post-commit clean check. The `--accept` caller keeps its existing `expected` set. Its silent skip of an ignored path becomes the shared one-line warning, which is an allowed change. The single-step and `--all` sweep callers pass: the plan file, the plan's `plan-details/<slug>/` directory, the archived plan and manifest when `--archive` completed the plan, and the paths changed since a baseline taken just before `run_step`. That baseline uses `git_state.changed_paths_or_none` for the changed paths. Rename origins come from a separate, additive rename-aware read of the same `git status --porcelain -z` output, added beside it in `git_state.py`; `changed_paths_or_none` keeps its current return value, so the test-authoring gate in `launcher.py` sees exactly what it sees today. The backend writes arbitrary code and nothing records those writes except this git delta. As a result, a file another process writes during the backend call is still indistinguishable from the step's own work. The residual is filed in BUG_BACKLOG.md in step 6 and is not tracked further here. Dirt left between steps, or dirt from before the baseline, is excluded. The git delta holds path names only, so it cannot tell whether the step edited a path that was already dirty at the baseline. Such a path is not in the footprint and stays uncommitted, and `run` names each path that was dirty at the baseline and is still dirty after the commit in a one-line warning (left uncommitted because it was dirty before the step; the step may also have edited it), so the exclusion is never silent and the warning claims no more than the record shows. When `changed_paths_or_none` returns `None` (git state unreadable) at the baseline or after the step, `run --commit` fails closed for that step. It makes no commit, exits non-zero naming the unreadable snapshot, and leaves the step work in the tree for `git reset` recovery. It never falls back to the whole tree. Both sides of a rename in the delta are footprint entries. The footprint takes the origin path of each rename record from that rename-aware read, so a staged `git mv a b` commits the deletion of `a` with `b`. `launcher.py`'s test-authoring delta gate is not touched. Destructive-operation disposition: an archive move during a completing step is still staged inside the footprint, and a failed commit still leaves that step's work for `git reset` recovery. Rewrite the `--commit` help text ('stage all changes (git add -A)') and regenerate `docs/cli/run.md`. Tests go in `tests/cli/test_run_cmd.py`: an unrelated file dirtied after the baseline is excluded only when it is outside the delta (pinning the known residual), a file dirty before the step is not committed, a file dirty before the step and still dirty after is left uncommitted and named in the warning, an unreadable git state at either snapshot makes no commit and exits non-zero, a staged rename inside the step commits both paths and leaves both clean, the archive move is committed, an `--accept` ignored path warns, and the plan file is clean after each green commit." carries refactor verb(s) ['move', 'rename'] and feature verb(s) ['add'] — likely two concerns in one step.
